title: What is known about 1RB0LB_1LC0RE_1LA1LD_0LC---_0RB0RF_1RE1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LB_1LC0RE_1LA1LD_0LC---_0RB0RF_1RE1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, and probably never halting. The run from blank tape is, provably, the orbit of a Collatz-like map E(a, m) → E(a', m') with m' ≈ 4m/3 and a counter a that changes by +6, −1 or +4 according to m mod 3 (Lean, kernel-checked for all a ≥ 1 and m ≥ 2). The machine can only halt if the counter runs out; Lean checks that it does not in the first 20,000 map steps (more than 105000 machine steps). The counter drifts up by 3 per step, so the chance that it ever comes back down to 0 is about 10−28,000: the same kind of question as Antihydra.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The E-step map, for every counter and gap
claims.text: With E(a, m) = 1 0 0 (10)^a 0^m E> 1 on blank tape: for a ≥ 1 and m ≥ 2 the machine goes to E(a+6, 4k+4) if m = 3k, to E(a−1, 4k+7) if m = 3k+1, and to E(a+4, 4k+4) if m = 3k+2, in exactly 4k²+23k+16a+94, 4k²+23k+28 and 4k²+23k+8a+56 steps. Proved from symbolic rules (a loop that turns three 0s of the gap into two 10, iterated by induction, and the three ends) for all values.

claims.title: The run from blank tape follows the map
claims.text: The machine reaches E(4, 124) at step 9,008, and from there the run is the orbit of (4, 124) under the map for as long as the counter stays positive. Hence: if the counter never runs out, the machine never halts.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1,000 map steps (more than 10<sup>250</sup> machine steps)
claims.text: The counter stays positive for the first 1,000 E-steps, evaluated by the kernel; the step count reached has more than 250 digits.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000 map steps (more than 10<sup>5000</sup> machine steps)
claims.text: The same check for 20,000 E-steps with native_decide; the counter is then 60,462.

claims.title: 10<sup>6</sup> map steps without the counter running out
claims.text: Python iterates the map (exact big integers) 10<sup>6</sup> steps past the E-event at step 1.08·10<sup>10</sup>; the counter never goes below 58. The map was also checked against direct simulation: 25 consecutive E-events of the run from blank tape (up to 1.1·10<sup>10</sup> steps, step counts exact) and 546 starts E(a, m) with 1 ≤ a ≤ 7, 2 ≤ m ≤ 79.

claims.title: Probviously non-halting: a random walk drifting away from 0
claims.text: If m mod 3 behaves like a fair three-sided die, the counter is a random walk with steps +6, −1, +4 (drift +3). The chance of ever coming down by d is about λ<sup>d</sup> with λ = 0.33489 the root in (0,1) of λ<sup>7</sup>+λ<sup>5</sup>+1 = 3λ: about 10<sup>−27.6</sup> from a = 58 at 1.08·10<sup>10</sup> steps and about 10<sup>−28,700</sup> from a = 60,462 where Lean leaves it. bbchallenge lists the machine as an Antihydra-like cryptid (Racheline, November 2024).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: it halts only if the counter of a Collatz-like orbit runs out (and then only in some cases: at a = 0 with m = 1 mod 3 some gaps halt, others turn into a translated cycler or restart the counter). Deciding this is a problem of the Antihydra kind.

explainer.lede: Probably never, but nobody can prove it. The machine keeps a number m (a gap of zeros) that grows by a factor 4/3 at each round, and a small counter that goes up or down depending on m mod 3. It can only stop if the counter runs out, and the counter is drifting upwards: a question of the same kind as the famous Antihydra.

facts.text: Every round E(a, m) → E(a', m') is proved in Lean for all a ≥ 1, m ≥ 2, with exact step counts.
No halt: the counter stays positive for 20,000 rounds (Lean, native_decide).
Chance that the counter ever runs out, if m mod 3 is like a fair die.

sections.heading: A gap that grows by 4/3 and a counter
html: Every so often the head stands in state E on the last 1 of the tape, and the tape is then just three pieces: 100, a counter of a copies of 10, and a gap of m zeros. Call this E(a, m).

<rect x="500" y="40" width="30" height="30" fill="var(--head)" fill-opacity=".25" stroke="var(--head)"/><text x="515" y="60" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg2)">1</text>
<text x="515" y="30" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--head)">E</text>
<text x="125" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--muted)">counter a</text><text x="350" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--muted)">gap m (grows by 4/3)</text>
</svg>

Between two such moments the head runs a loop at the right end: each round eats three 0s of the gap and writes two more 10 to the right of it. When fewer than three 0s are left, what is left over (m mod 3) decides what happens to the counter, and a final sweep turns the new 10s back into a longer gap. The result:

From blank tape the first such moment is E(4, 124) at step 9,008; then E(3, 171), E(9, 232), E(8, 315), …, E(58, 137,643) at step 10.8 billion. The gap grows like (4/3)n and the steps per round like the square of the gap, so the visited tape grows like the square root of the step count, and the counter, written in the cells at the far end, only very slowly.

sections.heading: Only if the counter runs out
html: The map works as stated whenever the counter is at least 1. So the machine can only halt if, at some round with m = 1 mod 3, the counter is already 0. (What happens then depends on m: some gaps halt the machine a few thousand steps later, others turn into a pattern that repeats forever while moving right, others restart a counter.)

The counter goes up by 6 or by 4 two times out of three and down by 1 one time out of three, if the remainders of the gap behave like a fair die, which is what they look like. A walk that drifts up by 3 per round almost never comes back: the chance of ever coming down by d is about 0.335d. From 58 that is 10−27.6, and after the 20,000 rounds that Lean checks the counter is 60,462.

This is the situation of Antihydra (a 6-state machine computing n → 3n/2 with a counter that goes +2 or −1 with the parity): proving that the counter never runs out would mean proving something about the long-run behaviour of n mod 3 under multiplication by 4/3, which is beyond current mathematics.

sections.heading: Proved in Lean: the map, and 10<sup>5000</sup> steps
html:
• lean/Rules.lean (generated by py/rules.py with the repository's symbolic simulator): the start of a round, one turn of the loop, and the three ends, each for all values of its variables.
  • lean/Map.lean: the loop iterated k times by induction and emap_sound, the map with its exact step counts for every a ≥ 1 and m ≥ 2.
  • lean/Orbit.lean: blank tape reaches E(4, 124) at step 9,008 (kernel); the run is then the orbit of the map (orbit_sound); it stays away from the boundary for 1,000 rounds (kernel, more than 10250 steps) and 20,000 rounds (native_decide, more than 105000 steps); and not_halts_of_good: a counter that never runs out means no halt.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.087). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).
After 109 steps the tape spans 42,637 cells (105 left of the start, 31,443 right), with a density of 1s of 0.465.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Antihydra-like: a gap m grows by 4/3 per step while a counter a moves by +6, -1 or +4 with m mod 3; it can only halt if the counter, now drifting up by 3 per step, ever runs out.
